## Real Data Analysis: Data Preparation and Variable Selection

Run the code below to prepare the real-world dataset and perform variable selection using stochastic search variable selection (SSVS). Set response_ID = 1 for mental illness or response_ID = 2 for alcohol and drug abuse. The code processes the covariates, selects relevant predictors using the joint \(S\) method, and saves the resulting predictor matrix for subsequent model fitting and analysis.


```{r}

response_name<-c("ML","AD")

####################
#User input
####################
#Set response_ID accordingly for corresponding response
# response_ID :1 = mental illness , response_ID :2 = alcohol & drug abuse
response_ID<- 
  ####################


data <- read.csv(file.path(path, "Real_data.csv"),check.names = FALSE)

response <- data[, c("Mental_illness", "Alcohol_&_drug_abuse")]

X <- data[, !names(data) %in% c("Mental_illness", "Alcohol_&_drug_abuse")]

X<-covariate_processing(X)

# Add intercept
X <- cbind(Intercept = 1, X)



y <- as.numeric(response[, response_ID]) #

# Recode response categories: (1,2)->1 ; 3->2 ; 4->3 ; else->4
y <- ifelse(y %in% c(1, 2), 1,
            ifelse(y == 3, 2,
                   ifelse(y == 4, 3, 4)))

category_name <- 1:4
k <- length(unique(na.omit(y)))

category_position <- lapply(
  1:k, function(j) which(y == j)
)


nit=50000
nmc=50000
nthin=10
tau2=.04^2
lamda2=10
proposal_step=.1

#selecting variables uses SSVS
set.seed(12345)
assign(paste("run_SSVS_Joint_S_",response_name[response_ID],sep=""), run_SSVS_Joint_S(X, y, nit, nmc, nthin,tau2,lamda2,proposal_step)  ) 

## ---------------------------
## Choose specific predictors selected from SSVS
## ---------------------------
varlist <- get(paste("run_SSVS_Joint_S_", response_name[response_ID], sep = ""))
X <- X[, varlist, drop = FALSE]
assign(paste("X_", response_name[response_ID], sep=""),X) #X_ML, X_AD

save(list = paste("X_", response_name[response_ID], sep = ""),
     file = file.path(path, paste("X_", response_name[response_ID], ".RData", sep = "")))

## ---------------------------
## Combine, clean, and finalize dataset
## ---------------------------

data <- data.frame(y, X)
data <- na.omit(data)

y <- data$y
X <- data[, -1]

x_tilda<- diag((k-1)) %x% as.matrix(X)

X1<-X

p<-ncol(X)


```




## Real Data Analysis: Model Fitting 
Run the code below to fit the proposed joint \(S\) multinomial probit model separately for mental illness and alcohol and drug abuse. The code obtains posterior samples, standardizes the regression coefficients. Ensure that the corresponding response and selected predictors are loaded before running each analysis.

```{r}

##############################
# for mental illness 
set.seed(12345)
MCMC_Joint_S_ML<-run_multinomial_univariate_mcmc(X, y,
                                                 nit=nit, nmc=nmc, nthin=nthin,
                                                 tau2=tau2,lamda2=lamda2,
                                                 proposal_step=proposal_step,
                                                 S_update_method = "joint",
                                                 R_update_method = "grid")

save(MCMC_Joint_S_ML,file = file.path(path, "MCMC_Joint_S_ML.RData"))


Joint_S_beta_ML<-MCMC_Joint_S_ML$beta_final_vector
Joint_S_sigma_ML<-MCMC_Joint_S_ML$sigma2_final
Joint_S_S_ML<-MCMC_Joint_S_ML$S_final
Joint_S_R_ML<-MCMC_Joint_S_ML$R_final


#Standardized the beta 
Joint_S_STD_beta_ML<- array(NA, c((k-1)*p, ncol(Joint_S_beta_ML)) )

for( i in 1:ncol(Joint_S_beta_ML)){
  
  mat_beta<-matrix(Joint_S_beta_ML[,i],ncol = p,byrow = T)
  
  Joint_S_STD_beta_ML[,i] <-  c(t(mat_beta / c(Joint_S_S_ML[,i])))
  
}






### mental illness  ###

set.seed(12345)
loglikelihood_ML <- sapply(seq_len(ncol(Joint_S_beta_ML)), function(i) {
  X_BETA_tilda <- colSums(t(x_tilda) * Joint_S_beta_ML[, i])
  X_BETA <- matrix(X_BETA_tilda, ncol = (k - 1))
  unlist(log_likelihood_mnp_1response(category_position, mu = X_BETA, Joint_S_sigma_ML[,, i])[2])
})


beta_bar<- apply(Joint_S_beta_ML,1,mean) 
sigma_bar<-apply(Joint_S_sigma_ML, c(1,2), mean)
X_BETA_tilda<-colSums(t(x_tilda)* c(beta_bar))   
X_BETA_bar<-matrix( X_BETA_tilda, ncol= (k-1) )


set.seed(12345)
D_theta_bar<- -2*unlist(log_likelihood_mnp_1response(category_position,mu=X_BETA_bar,sigma_bar)[2])
D_bar<- -2*mean(loglikelihood_ML)
p_D <- D_bar - D_theta_bar
BPIC_ML <- D_bar + 2 * p_D

print(BPIC_ML)



# for ordinal probit 
print( get_BPIC_ordinal_probit_model(X,y) )

###############################




###############################
# For alcohol & drug abuse
set.seed(12345)
MCMC_Joint_S_Alcohol<-run_multinomial_univariate_mcmc(X, y,
                                                      nit=nit, nmc=nmc, nthin=nthin,
                                                      tau2=tau2,lamda2=lamda2,
                                                      proposal_step=proposal_step,
                                                      S_update_method = "joint",
                                                      R_update_method = "grid")


save(MCMC_Joint_S_Alcohol,file = file.path(path, "MCMC_Joint_S_Alcohol.RData"))


Joint_S_beta_Alcohol<-MCMC_Joint_S_Alcohol$beta_final_vector
Joint_S_sigma_Alcohol<-MCMC_Joint_S_Alcohol$sigma2_final
Joint_S_S_Alcohol<-MCMC_Joint_S_Alcohol$S_final
Joint_S_R_Alcohol<-MCMC_Joint_S_Alcohol$R_final


#Standardized the beta 
Joint_S_STD_beta_Alcohol<- array(NA, c((k-1)*p, ncol(Joint_S_beta_Alcohol)) )

for( i in 1:ncol(Joint_S_beta_Alcohol)){
  
  mat_beta<-matrix(Joint_S_beta_Alcohol[,i],ncol = p,byrow = T)
  
  Joint_S_STD_beta_Alcohol[,i] <-  c(t(mat_beta / c(Joint_S_S_Alcohol[,i])))
  
}





### alcohol & drug abuse ###

set.seed(12345)
loglikelihood_AL <- sapply(seq_len(ncol(Joint_S_beta_Alcohol)), function(i) {
  X_BETA_tilda <- colSums(t(x_tilda) * Joint_S_beta_Alcohol[, i])
  X_BETA <- matrix(X_BETA_tilda, ncol = (k - 1))
  unlist(log_likelihood_mnp_1response(category_position, mu = X_BETA, Joint_S_sigma_Alcohol[,, i])[2])
})


beta_bar<- apply(Joint_S_beta_Alcohol,1,mean) 
sigma_bar<-apply(Joint_S_sigma_Alcohol, c(1,2), mean)
X_BETA_tilda<-colSums(t(x_tilda)* c(beta_bar))   
X_BETA_bar<-matrix( X_BETA_tilda, ncol= (k-1) )


set.seed(12345)
D_theta_bar<- -2*unlist(log_likelihood_mnp_1response(category_position,mu=X_BETA_bar,sigma_bar)[2])
D_bar<- -2*mean(loglikelihood_AL)
p_D <- D_bar - D_theta_bar
BPIC_AL <- D_bar + 2 * p_D

print(BPIC_AL)



# for ordinal probit 
print( get_BPIC_ordinal_probit_model(X,y) )

```




## Reproduce Table 5: Posterior Estimates of Standardized Regression Coefficients

Run the code below to reproduce Table 5, which summarizes the posterior median estimates and 95% highest posterior density (HPD) interval widths of the standardized regression coefficients for mental illness and alcohol and drug abuse. The results are presented separately for each response category, with predictors aligned across both outcomes for comparison.

```{r}

###########################################
# Code to generate Table 5
###########################################

Standardized_beta_median<-round(apply(Joint_S_STD_beta_ML,1,quantile,p=c(.5)),3)
Standardized_HPDI_beta<- round(hdi(t(Joint_S_STD_beta_ML)),3)

ML_med   <- matrix(Standardized_beta_median,      nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
ML_low   <- matrix(Standardized_HPDI_beta[1, ],   nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
ML_high  <- matrix(Standardized_HPDI_beta[2, ],   nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)



Standardized_beta_median_Alcohol<-round(apply(Joint_S_STD_beta_Alcohol,1,quantile,p=c(.5)),3)
Standardized_HPDI_beta_Alcohol<- round(hdi(t(Joint_S_STD_beta_Alcohol)),3)

AL_med   <- matrix(Standardized_beta_median_Alcohol,     nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
AL_low   <- matrix(Standardized_HPDI_beta_Alcohol[1, ],  nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
AL_high  <- matrix(Standardized_HPDI_beta_Alcohol[2, ],  nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)


### -----------------------------
### Helper function to format cell
### -----------------------------
fmt <- function(m, lo, hi){
  width <- round(hi - lo, 3)
  paste0(m, " (", width, ")")
}

### -----------------------------
### 1. Format ML table
### -----------------------------
ML_table <- matrix("", nrow = ncol(X_ML), ncol = 3)
for(i in 1:3){
  for(j in 1:ncol(X_ML)){
    ML_table[j, i] <- fmt(ML_med[i, j], ML_low[i, j], ML_high[i, j])
  }
}

predictors_ML <- colnames(X_ML)
rownames(ML_table) <- predictors_ML
colnames(ML_table) <- c("Cat1_ML","Cat2_ML","Cat3_ML")


### -----------------------------
### 2. Format Alcohol table
### -----------------------------
AL_table <- matrix("", nrow = ncol(X_AD), ncol = 3)
for(i in 1:3){
  for(j in 1:ncol(X_AD)){
    AL_table[j, i] <- fmt(AL_med[i, j], AL_low[i, j], AL_high[i, j])
  }
}

predictors_AL <- colnames(X_AD)
rownames(AL_table) <- predictors_AL
colnames(AL_table) <- c("Cat1_Alcohol","Cat2_Alcohol","Cat3_Alcohol")


### -----------------------------
### 3. Merge tables (align predictors)
### -----------------------------
ML_df <- cbind(Predictor = rownames(ML_table), ML_table)
AL_df <- cbind(Predictor = rownames(AL_table), AL_table)

Full_tab <- full_join(as.data.frame(ML_df),
                      as.data.frame(AL_df),
                      by = "Predictor")


print(Full_tab)
```




## Reproduce Table 6: Cross-Validation Results for Mental Illness and Alcohol and Drug Abuse

Run the code below to reproduce Table 6, which compares the observed category proportions with their corresponding 95% highest posterior density (HPD) predictive intervals. Set response_ID = 1 for mental illness and response_ID = 2 for alcohol and drug abuse, and rerun the corresponding data preparation steps for each outcome. The analysis considers covariate combinations with at least 30 observations and reports the results separately for both responses.
To obtain the corresponding results for the BN12 method, replace the run_multinomial_univariate_mcmc() function with run_multinomial_univariate_mcmc_BN12() with appropriate arguments

```{r}

#######################################################
## Code for generating Table 6
#######################################################


# For Mental illness

# set response_ID<-1 and run code lines from 30 to 86 
#you can skip line 67 if you already have the output

unq_row_of_X<-unique(as.matrix(X) )

# Step 1: Get counts
check_no_of_each_combination <- sapply(1:nrow(unq_row_of_X), function(i) {
  sum(rowSums(abs(t(t(X) - unq_row_of_X[i, ]))) == 0)
})

target_count <- 30   

# Step 3: Get the index (first match) of the row with target count
target_index <- which(check_no_of_each_combination >= target_count)  # in case of multiple matches

# Step 4: Extract the row
unq_row_of_X <- unq_row_of_X[target_index, , drop = FALSE]



test_X_list<-list()
test_Y_list<-list()
beta_final_vector_list<-list()
sigma2_final_list<-list()

for(cv in 1:nrow(unq_row_of_X)){
  
  
  # Get the first row of unq_row_of_X
  target_row <- unq_row_of_X[cv, ]
  
  # Find the matching row(s) in x1
  index <- which(apply(X1, 1, function(row) all(row == target_row)))
  
  test_data<- as.matrix( data[index,] )
  train_data<- as.matrix( data[-index,])
  
  
  X<- as.matrix( train_data[,-1])
  y<- as.numeric(train_data[,1])
  n<-length(y)
  
  
  
  X_test<- as.matrix( test_data[,-1])
  y_test<- as.numeric(test_data[,1])
  
  test_x_tilda<- diag((k-1)) %x% X_test 
  n_test<- length(y_test)
  
  
  set.seed(12345)
  MCMC_Joint_S_ML<-run_multinomial_univariate_mcmc(X, y,
                                                   nit=nit, nmc=nmc, nthin=nthin,
                                                   tau2=tau2,lamda2=lamda2,
                                                   proposal_step=proposal_step,
                                                   S_update_method = "joint",
                                                   R_update_method = "grid")
  
  
  
  Joint_S_beta_ML<-MCMC_Joint_S_ML$beta_final_vector
  Joint_S_sigma_ML<-MCMC_Joint_S_ML$sigma2_final
  Joint_S_S_ML<-MCMC_Joint_S_ML$S_final
  Joint_S_R_ML<-MCMC_Joint_S_ML$R_final
  
  
  
  
  test_X_list[[cv]]<-X_test  
  test_Y_list[[cv]]<-y_test
  beta_final_vector_list[[cv]]<-Joint_S_beta_ML
  sigma2_final_list[[cv]]<-Joint_S_sigma_ML
  
}


nsamples<-nmc/nthin

set.seed(12345)
estimated_PP_P<-list()

for(ll in 1:length(test_X_list)){
  
  test_x_tilda_P<- diag((k-1)) %x%  unique(test_X_list[[ll]])
  beta_final_vector_P<-beta_final_vector_list[[ll]]
  
  
  estimated_PP<-array(NA,c(1,k,nsamples))
  
  for(iter in 1: nsamples){
    test_X_BETA_P<-colSums(t(test_x_tilda_P)* c(beta_final_vector_P[,iter]))
    test_X_BETA_P<-matrix( test_X_BETA_P, ncol= (k-1))
    
    sigma2_final_list_P<-sigma2_final_list[[ll]][,,iter]
    
    estimated_PP[,,iter]<- apply(matrix(1:k,ncol=1),1,new_probability_mnp_1response,mu=test_X_BETA_P,sigma=sigma2_final_list_P,r=250,Halton_choice=FALSE)
    
  }
  
  estimated_PP_P[[ll]]<-estimated_PP
}





full_probability_mat<-abind(estimated_PP_P,along = 1)

# Pre-allocate
pred_lb_HPDI <- matrix(NA, nrow = dim(full_probability_mat)[1], ncol = dim(full_probability_mat)[2])
pred_ub_HPDI <- matrix(NA, nrow = dim(full_probability_mat)[1], ncol = dim(full_probability_mat)[2])

# Loop over rows and categories
for(i in 1:dim(full_probability_mat)[1]) {
  for(j in 1:dim(full_probability_mat)[2]) {
    draws <- full_probability_mat[i, j, ]
    
    # 95% HDI
    hdi_vals <- hdi(draws, credMass = 0.95)
    pred_lb_HPDI[i, j] <- round(hdi_vals[1],3)
    pred_ub_HPDI[i, j] <- round(hdi_vals[2],3)
  }
}




final_y_test<-unlist(test_Y_list)
final_x_test<-do.call(rbind, test_X_list)


bbb<-unique(final_x_test)
yy<-list()


for(i in 1:nrow(bbb))
{
  yy[[i]]<-final_y_test[which(rowSums(abs(t(t(final_x_test)-bbb[i,])))==0)]
}


test_proportion_of_success<-matrix(NA,ncol=k,nrow=nrow(bbb))
for(i in 1:nrow(bbb))
{
  for(j in 1:k )
  {
    test_proportion_of_success[i,j]<- sum((yy[[i]])==j)/length(yy[[i]])
  }
  
}

colnames(test_proportion_of_success)<-c("Percent_of_1","Percent_of_2","Percent_of_3","Percent_of_4")



#####################################
# To generate 1st block of Table 6 
#####################################

# Combine components into "p (lb, ub)"
p  <- round(test_proportion_of_success, 3)
lb <- round(pred_lb_HPDI, 3)
ub <- round(pred_ub_HPDI, 3)

cell <- matrix("", nrow = nrow(p), ncol = ncol(p))

for (i in 1:nrow(p)) {
  for (j in 1:ncol(p)) {
    cell[i, j] <- sprintf("%0.3f (%0.3f, %0.3f)", p[i,j], lb[i,j], ub[i,j])
  }
}

colnames(cell) <- c("Category 0", "Category 1", "Category 2", "Category 3")


print(unq_row_of_X)

# Print nicely in R console
kable(cell, align = "c", caption = "cross-validation output for perception of Mental Illness")








#############################
# For Alcohol & Drug Abuse

#you can skip line 67 if you already have the output
```
